text: EX-10.1 2 ex10-1.htm EX-10.1 Exhibit 10.1 PURSUANT TO ITEM 601(b)(10)(iv) OF REGULATION S-K, CERTAIN IDENTIFIED INFORMATION HAS BEEN OMITTED FROM THIS EXHIBIT BECAUSE IT IS NOT MATERIAL AND IS THE TYPE THAT THE REGISTRANT TREATS AS PRIVATE OR CONFIDENTIAL. The original agreement is in Chinese. This English translation is provided for reference only. AI NOSE EQUIPMENT SALE AND PURCHASE AGREEMENT (Second Batch: 5,000 Units) This AI NOSE Equipment Sale and Purchase Agreement (the “Agreement”) is entered into by and between the following parties on the 12th day of November, ROC Year 115: Party A (Buyer) ASE Technology Holding Co., Ltd. Uniform Business No.: 29187308 Registered Address: _______________________________ Representative / Authorized Signatory: See signature block Party B (Seller) Ainos, Inc. Taiwan Branch (USA) Uniform Business No.: 58184202 Address: 10F.-2, No. 66, Shengyi 5th Road, Zhubei City, Hsinchu County Representative / Authorized Signatory: See signature block Party A and Party B are each individually referred to as a “Party” and collectively as the “Parties.” The Parties agree as follows with respect to the sale and purchase, delivery, and warranty of the AI NOSE equipment: Article 1 Subject Matter of Sale and Purchase 1. Party B agrees to sell, and Party A agrees to purchase, a total of 5,000 units of AI NOSE equipment (the “Equipment”). 2. The model, specifications, accessories, software version, delivery locations, and phased delivery arrangements for the Equipment shall be as set forth in the appendices to this Agreement, in documents confirmed in writing by both Parties, or in individual delivery notices issued by Party A. 3. This Agreement is an outright, one-time sale and purchase of equipment and does not constitute a lease, loan for use, or other arrangement for rights of use. Article 2 Price and Taxes 1. The unit price of the Equipment is US$[***] per unit. 2. The total purchase price is nine million U.S. dollars (US$9,000,000), being [***] units × US$[***]. 3. Business tax, import duties and fees, and other taxes required by law, whether included in or excluded from the foregoing price, shall be handled in accordance with the transaction structure of the original lease agreement and applicable laws and regulations. If business tax is required by law to be charged separately, Party A shall pay it separately against a lawful supporting document issued by Party B. Article 3 Payment Terms 1. Deposit: Within sixty (60) days after the date this Agreement is signed, Party A shall pay fifty percent (50%) of the total purchase price, namely four million five hundred thousand U.S. dollars (US$4,500,000). 2. Balance: After Party B has completed delivery of all of the Equipment, Party B may submit delivery documents and billing documents to invoice Party A for the remaining fifty percent (50%) of the total purchase price, namely four million five hundred thousand U.S. dollars (US$4,500,000). Party A shall pay the balance in accordance with such delivery and billing documents. 3. The total of 5,000 units of Equipment sold by Party B to Party A under this Agreement shall be delivered to the following facilities in the following quantities: [***] units to ASE Kaohsiung Plant, [***]) units to ASE Chungli Plant, and [***] units to SPIL Plant. Party A shall notify Party B in writing of the specific delivery address and receiving contact for each facility. 4. Party A shall make payment by wire transfer to the bank account designated by Party B in writing. Party A shall bear the remittance fees. 5. Annual Maintenance Fee: Starting on the day following the first anniversary of the delivery acceptance date for each unit of Equipment (i.e., beginning in the second year), for as long as Party A owns and uses the Equipment, Party A shall pay Party B an annual maintenance fee of [***] per unit per year. The fee includes platform usage fees and technical updates and AI algorithm upgrade services, and is consideration for Party B’s provision of annual maintenance services for that Equipment. The maintenance year for each unit shall be calculated separately from its delivery acceptance date. Article 4 Delivery 1. The delivery schedule, batches, locations, and on-site contacts shall be separately confirmed in writing by the Parties in accordance with the actual deployment plan. 2. At delivery of each batch of Equipment, Party B shall provide documents sufficient to evidence the quantity and fact of delivery, including a shipping document, delivery acceptance receipt, or other delivery document adopted by the Parties. 3. The risk of loss of or damage to the Equipment shall pass to Party A when each batch is delivered to the location designated by Party A and accepted by signature. Title shall pass when Party A has paid all amounts due under this Agreement in full. 4. Party A’s acceptance signature confirms delivery of the Equipment and quantity and does not affect Party A’s warranty rights under Article 6 for defects not caused by human action during the warranty period. Article 5 Installation, Configuration, and Cooperation 1. Delivery of the Equipment includes installation, initial configuration, connection, or deployment services for the Equipment to be provided by Party B. The scope and on-site conditions shall be as set forth in an appendix or in content confirmed in writing by the Parties. 2. Party A shall provide reasonably necessary site access permits, premises, power, network access, installation locations, and other on-site cooperation. Any delay caused by Party A’s premises or cooperation arrangements not being ready shall not constitute a delay in delivery by Party B. Article 6 Warranty 1. The warranty period for the Equipment is one year, calculated separately for each unit from its delivery acceptance date. 2. During the warranty period, if the Equipment malfunctions, is damaged, or fails to conform to the agreed specifications for reasons not caused by human action, Party B shall be responsible for inspection and repair or, in its reasonable judgment, replacement with equipment or components of equivalent function, without charging additional repair or replacement fees. 3. The following are outside the scope of the free warranty: improper use by Party A or a third party; unauthorized disassembly or modification; use contrary to operating requirements; external impact; abnormal environmental conditions; or other causes attributable to Party A. If Party B provides repairs, it may quote separately for them. 4. Party B’s warranty obligation shall, as a general rule, be limited to reasonably repairing or replacing the Equipment; provided, however, that this shall not apply to liability arising from Party B’s willful misconduct or gross negligence, or liability that may not be limited by law. Article 7 Software, Data, and Intellectual Property Rights 1. The subject matter of sale and purchase under this Agreement is ownership of the Equipment. Intellectual property rights in the AI NOSE-related software, algorithms, models, cloud platform, databases, firmware, technical documentation, and updates thereto shall remain with Party B or its licensors. Copyright and related intellectual property rights in programs and software related to the Equipment belong to Party B. Party B hereby permanently and irrevocably grants Party A a perpetual, royalty-free license, for so long as Party A owns the Equipment, to use them to the extent necessary to use, maintain, or improve the Equipment. 2. Party A may use the accompanying software only to the extent necessary for its internal operations and normal use of the Equipment. Without Party B’s prior written consent, Party A may not reverse engineer, decompile, copy, rent, sublicense, or provide it for use by any third party. 3. In addition to the annual equipment maintenance under Clause 5 of Article 3, if the Parties have any other service needs or need for annual technical support, they shall separately agree in writing on the service scope and fees; such services are not automatically included by virtue of the outright purchase of the Equipment. 4. The Parties agree that ownership of samples obtained by the Equipment at Party A’s premises through collection and testing of gases, or data generated thereby (the “Party A Data”), shall belong to Party A. Party B may analyze or use Party A Data only for the purpose of performing its obligations under this Agreement. Party B may not provide Party A Data to any other person without Party A’s prior written consent. Party B shall establish reasonable safeguards to ensure that others cannot directly obtain Party A Data stored on Party B’s hardware. Article 8 Confidentiality Each Party shall keep confidential any non-public technical, business, pricing, deployment, and operational information it obtains in connection with this Agreement and shall not disclose such information to any third party, except as required by law, a competent authority, or a court, or with the prior written consent of the disclosing Party. The obligations under this Article shall remain effective after termination or completion of this Agreement. Article 9 Force Majeure Neither Party shall be liable for delay when it is delayed in or unable to perform due to a natural disaster, war, government prohibition, major infectious disease, supply chain interruption, transportation interruption, or other event not reasonably within its control. The affected Party shall notify the other Party as soon as practicable and take reasonable measures to mitigate the impact. Article 10 Breach and Termination 1. If either Party materially breaches this Agreement and fails to cure the breach within thirty (30) days within thirty (30) day cure period specified in a written notice, the other Party may terminate this Agreement and seek damages in accordance with law. 2. Termination of this Agreement shall not affect payment obligations accrued before termination, confidentiality obligations, intellectual property rights, or other provisions that by their nature should survive. Article 11 Limitation of Liability Except for liability arising from willful misconduct, gross negligence, infringement of intellectual property rights, breach of confidentiality obligations, or liability that may not be limited by law, neither Party shall be liable to the other for indirect, incidental, special, or consequential damages, lost profits, or data loss. Party B’s aggregate liability under this Agreement shall be capped at the price actually paid by Party A for the Equipment giving rise to the liability. Article 12 Notices Notices under this Agreement shall be in writing and delivered personally, by registered mail, courier, or to the email address designated by the Parties, to the contact information stated in this Agreement or subsequently updated in writing. Article 13 Governing Law and Jurisdiction The interpretation, validity, and performance of this Agreement shall be governed by the laws of the Republic of China. Any dispute arising out of or in connection with this Agreement shall first be resolved through good-faith negotiations between the Parties. If negotiations fail, the competent court shall be determined in accordance with the jurisdiction provision of the original lease agreement. Article 14 Miscellaneous 1. This Agreement and its appendices constitute the entire agreement between the Parties with respect to the sale and purchase of the Equipment. In the event of any inconsistency between this Agreement and prior oral or written discussions concerning the same batch of Equipment, this Agreement shall prevail. 2. Any addition to, deletion from, or amendment of this Agreement shall be made in a written instrument signed by duly authorized representatives of both Parties. 3. Neither Party may assign all of its rights and obligations under this Agreement to a third party without the other Party’s prior written consent; provided, however, that this restriction shall not apply to a transfer by reason of corporate reorganization, merger, or succession by operation of law. 4. If any provision of this Agreement is determined to be invalid, the validity of the remaining provisions shall not be affected. 5. This Agreement may be executed in paper or electronic form and in multiple counterparts. Each counterpart shall be an original, and all counterparts together shall constitute one and the same instrument. 6. Party A may, by written notice to Party B, designate one or more of Party A’s subsidiaries to participate in this Agreement (each, a “Designated Subsidiary”). The notice shall state the name, uniform business number or other registration identification information, contact information, quantity of Equipment involved, and scope of rights and obligations to be assumed by each Designated Subsidiary. Upon joining under this paragraph, references in this Agreement to “Party A,” “Party,” and “Parties” shall, to the extent applicable and within the designated scope, include the Designated Subsidiary. A Designated Subsidiary may directly assert against Party B the rights to delivery, installation, software license, warranty, and maintenance relating to the Equipment allocated to it, and shall assume the corresponding obligations concerning payment, on-site cooperation, use restrictions, and confidentiality. Party B agrees that a Designated Subsidiary may use the related software and platform within the scope provided in this Agreement, and such use shall not be deemed sublicensing or provision for use by a third party prohibited under Article 7. Samples and data from a Designated Subsidiary’s premises shall also constitute “Party A Data” under Article 7, shall be owned by that Designated Subsidiary, and shall be subject to the use restrictions and protection obligations in that Article. Party A and a Designated Subsidiary may disclose confidential information to each other to the extent necessary to perform this Agreement, and the receiving party shall remain subject to the confidentiality obligations under Article 8. The joinder of a Designated Subsidiary shall not increase the total quantity of Equipment or total purchase price under this Agreement, nor change the original payment deadlines, title transfer conditions, or other transaction terms. The risk of loss of or damage to, and title to, Equipment within the designated scope shall pass to the applicable Designated Subsidiary at the times specified in Article 4. Payment by Party A or a Designated Subsidiary of the same amount payable shall discharge that payment obligation to the extent paid, and duplicate payment may not be demanded. Unless Party B otherwise agrees in writing, Party A shall not be released from its existing obligations under this Agreement by the joinder of a Designated Subsidiary, nor shall Party A thereby assume joint and several or guarantee liability for any new obligations separately incurred by the Designated Subsidiary. Party A and a Designated Subsidiary may not recover more than once for the same loss. The liability limitation in Article 11 shall aggregate related claims of Party A and the Designated Subsidiary, and the “price actually paid” referred to therein shall include the price actually paid by Party A and the Designated Subsidiary for the Equipment giving rise to the liability. The joinder of a Designated Subsidiary and its assumption of rights and obligations within the designated scope shall be an exception to paragraph 3 of this Article. The following is the signature page; the body ends here. SIGNATURE PAGE Party A (Buyer) Party B (Seller) ASE Technology Holding Co., Ltd. Ainos, Inc. Taiwan Branch (USA) Representative: /s/ Tien Wu Representative: /s/ Chun-Hsien Tsai Title: COO Title: CEO Date: 2026.11.12 Date: 2026.11.12

title: AppTech Payments Corp.
text: EX-10.1 2 apptech_ex1001.htm PROMISSORY NOTE, DATED NOVEMBER 13, 2026, Exhibit 10.1 PROMISSORY NOTE Principal Amount: $500,000.00 Date: November 13, 2026 FOR VALUE RECEIVED, the undersigned ("Borrower") hereby promises to pay to the Suzanne D. Lord Spousal Estate Reduction Trust dated January 17, 2025 ("Lender"), or its permitted assigns, the principal sum of Five Hundred Thousand Dollars ($500,000.00) , together with interest thereon, pursuant to the terms set forth below. The proceeds of this Note shall be used by the Borrower for short-term working capital and general corporate purposes. 1. Principal The Borrower acknowledges receipt of the principal amount of $500,000.00 . 2. Interest The outstanding principal balance shall bear interest at the rate of nine percent (9.00%) per annum , calculated on the basis of a 365-day year and the actual number of days elapsed. No payments of principal or interest shall be due prior to the Maturity Date. 3. Maturity All outstanding principal together with all accrued and unpaid interest shall be due and payable on the date that is ninety (90) days from the date of this Note (the "Maturity Date"). 1 4. Prepayment The Borrower may prepay this Note, in whole or in part, at any time without premium or penalty; provided that any prepayment shall include all accrued but unpaid interest through the date of payment. 5. Events of Default Each of the following shall constitute an Event of Default: 1. Failure to pay any amount due under this Note on the Maturity Date. 2. The Borrower files for, or becomes subject to, any bankruptcy, insolvency, or receivership proceeding. 3. The Borrower materially breaches any provision of this Note and fails to cure such breach within ten (10) business days after written notice from the Lender. Upon the occurrence of an Event of Default, the Lender may declare all outstanding principal and accrued interest immediately due and payable. 6. Waivers The Borrower waives presentment, demand, notice of dishonor, protest, and all other notices or demands in connection with the enforcement of this Note. 7. Governing Law This Note shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the State of California, without regard to its conflict of law principles. 8. Assignment This Note shall be binding upon and inure to the benefit of the Borrower and the Lender and their respective successors and permitted assigns. 9. Amendments No amendment, modification, or waiver of any provision of this Note shall be effective unless made in writing and signed by both the Borrower and the Lender. 10. Entire Agreement This Note constitutes the entire agreement between the parties concerning the subject matter hereof and supersedes all prior discussions or agreements relating thereto. 2 IN WITNESS WHEREOF The parties have executed this Promissory Note as of the date first written above. BORROWER AppTech Payments Corporation /s/ Felipe Corrado, IV By: Felipe Corrado, IV Title: interim Chief Executive Officer and Chief Financial Officer Date: November 13, 2026 LENDER Suzanne D. Lord Spousal Estate Reduction Trust dated January 17, 2025 Name: Albert L. Lord, Jr. Trustee Date: November 13, 2026 3

text: EX-10.1 7 dp256691_ex1001.htm EXHIBIT 10.1 Exhibit 10.1 FORM OF TERMINATION AGREEMENT This termination agreement (this “ Termination Agreement ”) with respect to the Call Option Confirmations (as defined below) is made as of [●], 20[●] between [●] (“ Dealer ”)[, represented by [●] (“ Agent ”) as its agent,] and Integer Holdings Corporation (“ Counterparty ”), a Delaware corporation. WHEREAS, Counterparty issued $500,000,000 aggregate principal amount of 2.125% Convertible Senior Notes due 2028 (the “ Convertible Notes ”) pursuant to an Indenture dated as of February 3, 2023 (the “ Indenture ”), between Counterparty and Wilmington Trust, National Association, as trustee; WHEREAS, Dealer and Counterparty are parties to the base capped call option transaction (as amended, modified or supplemented, the “ Base Call Option Transaction ”) evidenced by the letter agreement and side letter between Dealer and Counterparty, dated as of January 31, 2023 (as amended, modified or supplemented, the “ Base Call Option Confirmation ”), and the additional capped call option transaction (as amended, modified or supplemented, the “ Additional Call Option Transaction ” and, together with the Base Call Option Transaction, the “ Call Option Transactions ”) evidenced by the letter agreement and side letter between Dealer and Counterparty, dated as of February 1, 2023 (as amended, modified or supplemented, the “ Additional Call Option Confirmation ” and, together with the Base Call Option Confirmation, the “ Call Option Confirmations ”); WHEREAS , pursuant to the Agreement and Plan of Merger, dated as of August 2, 2026 (the “ Merger Agreement ”), by and among Counterparty, Armstrong Parent, Inc., a Delaware corporation (“ Parent ”), and Armstrong Bidco, Inc., a Delaware corporation and a wholly owned subsidiary of Parent (“ Merger Sub ”), and upon the terms and subject to the conditions therein, at the Effective Time (as defined in the Merger Agreement) (the “ Effective Time ”), Merger Sub will merge with and into Counterparty (the “ Merger ”), with Counterparty surviving the Merger as a wholly owned subsidiary of Parent; and WHEREAS, Counterparty has requested the full termination of all remaining call options under both the Base Call Option Transaction and the Additional Call Option Transaction in connection with the consummation of the Merger. NOW, THEREFORE, in consideration of their mutual covenants contained herein and for other good and valuable consideration, the receipt and sufficiency of which are hereby acknowledged, the parties hereto, intending to be legally bound, hereby mutually covenant and agree as follows: 1. Defined Terms. Any capitalized term not otherwise defined herein shall have the meaning set forth for such term in the Call Option Confirmations. 2. Termination of Transactions and Confirmations. Notwithstanding anything to the contrary in the Call Option Confirmations, Counterparty and Dealer agree that, upon the occurrence of the Closing (as defined in the Merger Agreement), (i) the Base Call Option Transaction shall automatically terminate and all of the respective rights and obligations of the parties under the Base Call Option Confirmation shall be terminated, cancelled and extinguished, (ii) the Additional Call Option Transaction shall automatically terminate and all of the respective rights and obligations of the parties under the Additional Call Option Confirmation shall be terminated, cancelled and extinguished and (iii) in consideration of the foregoing, Dealer shall pay to Page 1 Counterparty, in immediately available funds to the account specified in Section 8 below, cash in US Dollars in an amount equal to $[●] (the “ Call Option Unwind Amount ”) no later than close of business on the Closing Date, if notified of the Closing Date on or before 2 p.m. on the date thereof, or by 11:00 a.m. (New York City time) on the first Business Day following the Closing Date if notified after 2 p.m. (each as defined in the Merger Agreement). 3. Notification of Closing Date. Counterparty shall notify Dealer not later than 5:00 p.m., New York City time, on the Closing Date (as defined in the Merger Agreement) of the occurrence thereof, which notice shall be provided via email to the email address set forth in Section 7 below. 4. Further Adjustments; Termination. (a) Dealer agrees that it shall not, prior to any termination of this Termination Agreement, modify, amend, adjust, cancel or terminate, or suspend its performance under, any of the Call Option Confirmations, including but not limited to declaring an Early Termination Date thereunder. (b) If the Merger Agreement is terminated or amended in any respect that could reasonably be expected to have a material effect on the determination of the Call Option Unwind Amount, this Termination Agreement shall immediately terminate and shall be of no force and effect, no Call Option Unwind Amount shall be owed hereunder, and each of the Call Option Confirmations shall remain in full force and effect pursuant to the terms thereof in effect immediately prior to the execution of this Termination Agreement. 5. Representations and Warranties of Counterparty and Dealer. Each of Counterparty and Dealer represents and warrants to the other party on the date hereof that: (a) it is duly organized and validly existing under the laws of the jurisdiction of its organization or incorporation and, if relevant under such laws, in good standing; (b) it has the power to execute this Termination Agreement and any other documentation relating to this Termination Agreement, to deliver this Termination Agreement and each such other document relating thereto (if any) and to perform its obligations hereunder and thereunder (as applicable) and has taken all necessary action to authorize such execution, delivery and performance; (c) such execution, delivery and performance do not violate or conflict with any law applicable to it, any provision of its constitutional documents, any order or judgment of any court or other agency of government applicable to it or any of its assets or any contractual restriction binding on or affecting it or any of its assets; (d) all governmental and other consents that are required to have been obtained by it with respect to this Termination Agreement have been obtained and are in full force and effect and all conditions of any such consents have been complied with; (e) its obligations under this Termination Agreement constitute its legal, valid and binding obligations, enforceable in accordance with their respective terms (subject to applicable bankruptcy, reorganization, insolvency, moratorium or similar laws affecting creditors' rights generally and subject, as to enforceability, to equitable principles of general application (regardless of whether enforcement is sought in a proceeding in equity or at law)); and Page 2 (f) on the date hereof, it remains a party to the Call Option Transactions to the full extent as on the date of execution thereof and it has not assigned, purported to assign or made any attempt to assign, any interest in the Call Option Transactions to any third party. 6. Representations and Warranties of Counterparty. Counterparty represents and warrants to Dealer on the date hereof that: (a) it is not entering into this Termination Agreement to create actual or apparent trading activity in the Shares (or any security convertible into or exchangeable for the Shares, including the Convertible Notes) or to raise or depress or otherwise manipulate the price of the Shares (or any security convertible into or exchangeable for the Shares, including the Convertible Notes) or otherwise in violation of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, as amended; and (b) it (i) is capable of evaluating investment risks independently, both in general and with regard to all transactions and investment strategies involving a security or securities; (ii) will exercise independent judgment in evaluating the recommendations of any broker-dealer or its associated persons, unless it has otherwise notified the broker-dealer in writing; and (iii) has total assets of at least $50 million. 7. Notices. For purposes of this Termination Agreement, the addresses for notices or communications to the parties shall be: (a) Counterparty: Integer Holdings Corporation 5830 Granite Parkway, Suite 1150 Plano, Texas 75024 (b) Dealer: [●] [●] Attention: [●] Email: [●] 8. Account Details. For purposes of this Termination Agreement, the account for payments to Counterparty shall be: Page 3 9. Governing Law. THIS TERMINATION AGREEMENT AND ANY CLAIM, CONTROVERSY OR DISPUTE ARISING UNDER OR RELATED TO THIS TERMINATION AGREEMENT SHALL BE GOVERNED BY THE LAWS OF THE STATE OF NEW YORK. THE PARTIES HERETO IRREVOCABLY SUBMIT TO THE EXCLUSIVE JURISDICTION OF THE COURTS OF THE STATE OF NEW YORK AND THE UNITED STATES COURT FOR THE SOUTHERN DISTRICT OF NEW YORK IN CONNECTION WITH ALL MATTERS RELATING HERETO AND WAIVE ANY OBJECTION TO THE LAYING OF VENUE IN, ANY CLAIM OF INCONVENIENT FORUM WITH RESPECT TO, THESE COURTS. 10. Waiver of Trial by Jury. EACH OF COUNTERPARTY AND DEALER HEREBY IRREVOCABLY WAIVES (ON ITS OWN BEHALF AND, TO THE EXTENT PERMITTED BY APPLICABLE LAW, ON BEHALF OF ITS STOCKHOLDERS) ALL RIGHT TO TRIAL BY JURY IN ANY ACTION, PROCEEDING OR COUNTERCLAIM (WHETHER BASED ON CONTRACT, TORT OR OTHERWISE) ARISING OUT OF OR RELATING TO THE TRANSACTIONS CONTEMPLATED HEREBY OR THE ACTIONS OF DEALER OR ITS AFFILIATES IN THE NEGOTIATION, PERFORMANCE OR ENFORCEMENT HEREOF. 11. Amendment; Continuing Effect. This Termination Agreement may not be modified, amended or supplemented, except in a written instrument signed by each party hereto. Except as set forth herein, all other terms of the Call Option Transactions and provisions of the Call Option Confirmations shall remain and continue in full force and effect unless and until terminated in accordance with Section 2 hereof, and are hereby confirmed in all respects. 12. Counterparts. This Termination Agreement may be executed by any one or more of the parties hereto in any number of counterparts, each of which shall be deemed to be an original, but all such counterparts shall together constitute one and the same instrument. Counterparts may be delivered via facsimile, electronic mail (including any electronic signature covered by the U.S. federal ESIGN Act of 2000, Uniform Electronic Transactions Act, the Electronic Signatures and Records Act or other applicable law, e.g., www.docusign.com) or other transmission method and any counterpart so delivered shall be deemed to have been duly and validly delivered and be valid and effective for all purposes. [Remainder of page intentionally left blank] Page 4 IN WITNESS WHEREOF the parties have executed this Termination Agreement with effect from the date specified on the first page of this Termination Agreement. [DEALER] By: Name: Title: Date: INTEGER HOLDINGS CORPORATION By: Name: Title: Date: [AGENT, as agent for DEALER] By: Name: Title: Date: Page 5

Counterparty represents and warrants to Dealer on the date hereof that: (a) it is not entering into this Termination Agreement to create actual or apparent trading activity in the Shares (or any security convertible into or exchangeable for the Shares, including the Convertible Notes) or to raise or depress or otherwise manipulate the price of the Shares (or any security convertible into or exchangeable for the Shares, including the Convertible Notes) or otherwise in violation of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, as amended; and (b) it (i) is capable of evaluating investment risks independently, both in general and with regard to all transactions and investment strategies involving a security or securities; (ii) will exercise independent judgment in evaluating the recommendations of any broker-dealer or its associated persons, unless it has otherwise notified the broker-dealer in writing; and (iii) has total assets of at least $50 million. 7. Notices. For purposes of this Termination Agreement, the addresses for notices or communications to the parties shall be: (a) Counterparty: Integer Holdings Corporation 5830 Granite Parkway, Suite 1150 Plano, Texas 75024 (b) Dealer: [●] [●] Attention: [●] Email: [●] 8. Account Details. For purposes of this Termination Agreement, the account for payments to Counterparty shall be: Page 3 9. Governing Law. THIS TERMINATION AGREEMENT AND ANY CLAIM, CONTROVERSY OR DISPUTE ARISING UNDER OR RELATED TO THIS TERMINATION AGREEMENT SHALL BE GOVERNED BY THE LAWS OF THE STATE OF NEW YORK. THE PARTIES HERETO IRREVOCABLY SUBMIT TO THE EXCLUSIVE JURISDICTION OF THE COURTS OF THE STATE OF NEW YORK AND THE UNITED STATES COURT FOR THE SOUTHERN DISTRICT OF NEW YORK IN CONNECTION WITH ALL MATTERS RELATING HERETO AND WAIVE ANY OBJECTION TO THE LAYING OF VENUE IN, ANY CLAIM OF INCONVENIENT FORUM WITH RESPECT TO, THESE COURTS. 10. Waiver of Trial by Jury. EACH OF COUNTERPARTY AND DEALER HEREBY IRREVOCABLY WAIVES (ON ITS OWN BEHALF AND, TO THE EXTENT PERMITTED BY APPLICABLE LAW, ON BEHALF OF ITS STOCKHOLDERS) ALL RIGHT TO TRIAL BY JURY IN ANY ACTION, PROCEEDING OR COUNTERCLAIM (WHETHER BASED ON CONTRACT, TORT OR OTHERWISE) ARISING OUT OF OR RELATING TO THE TRANSACTIONS CONTEMPLATED HEREBY OR THE ACTIONS OF DEALER OR ITS AFFILIATES IN THE NEGOTIATION, PERFORMANCE OR ENFORCEMENT HEREOF. 11. Amendment; Continuing Effect. This Termination Agreement may not be modified, amended or supplemented, except in a written instrument signed by each party hereto. Except as set forth herein, all other terms of the Call Option Transactions and provisions of the Call Option Confirmations shall remain and continue in full force and effect unless and until terminated in accordance with Section 2 hereof, and are hereby confirmed in all respects. 12. Counterparts. This Termination Agreement may be executed by any one or more of the parties hereto in any number of counterparts, each of which shall be deemed to be an original, but all such counterparts shall together constitute one and the same instrument. Counterparts may be delivered via facsimile, electronic mail (including any electronic signature covered by the U.S. federal ESIGN Act of 2000, Uniform Electronic Transactions Act, the Electronic Signatures and Records Act or other applicable law, e.g., www.docusign.com) or other transmission method and any counterpart so delivered shall be deemed to have been duly and validly delivered and be valid and effective for all purposes.
