text: EX-10.2 5 ea031248601ex10-2.htm LETTER AGREEMENT, DATED NOVEMBER 12, 2026, BY AND BETWEEN ALLARITY THERAPEUTICS, INC. AND STREETERVILLE CAPITAL, LLC Exhibit 10.2 STREETERVILLE CAPITAL, LLC November 12, 2026 Allarity Therapeutics, Inc. Attn: Thomas Jensen tjensen@allarity.com Re: Conditional Consent to Future Use of ATM Dear Thomas: This letter agreement (this “ Letter Agreement ”) is entered into by and between Streeterville Capital, LLC, a Utah limited liability company (“ Investor ”), and Allarity Therapeutics, Inc., a Delaware corporation (“ Company ”), in connection with Company’s Certificate of Designation of Preferences and Rights of Series B Preferred Stock (the “ Series B Certificate ”). Reference is also made to that certain Exchange Agreement by and between Investor and Company of even date herewith (the “ Exchange Agreement ”). Capitalized terms used but not otherwise defined herein will have the meanings ascribed to such terms in the Series B Certificate. Investor and Company hereby agree as follows: 1. Conditional Consent to Use of ATM . (a) Investor hereby grants its consent for Company to sell shares of its Common Stock under any future at-the-market (ATM) trading facility, notwithstanding Section 10(e) of the Series B Certificate, subject to the terms of this Section 1. The foregoing consent may be revoked by Investor at any time by delivering written notice of such to Company. (b) For each week that Company sells Common Shares under its ATM, Company shall pay Investor, by wire transfer of immediately available funds, an amount equal to thirty-three percent (33%) of the net proceeds from all sales settled during that week (each, a “ Sweep Payment ”). (c) Investor may elect, by written notice delivered at any time and from time to time, to apply any Sweep Payment, in whole or in part, to either or both of the following: i. redemption of shares of Series B Stock held by Investor, at the Redemption Price set forth in the Series B Certificate; and ii. repayment of the outstanding balance of the Note (as defined in the Exchange Agreement), as elected by Investor. (d) If no election is in effect, unless the redemption described in clause (i) is not permitted by applicable law or the Series B Certificate, the Sweep Payment shall be applied under clause (i). Once the Note is paid in full or Investor no longer owns and shares of Series B Stock, the entire Sweep Payment shall be applied to the other. (e) Upon Investor’s request, if any sales were made pursuant to the ATM during the preceding week, Company shall provide Investor with a report detailing the aggregate number of shares sold and gross proceeds received from such sales during such week. (f) Any failure to make a Sweep Payment when due shall be considered an event of default under the Note and the Series B Certificate. (g) This consent is limited to the matters expressly set forth herein. It does not waive any other provision of any other agreement between the parties or any default thereunder. 2. B Note Exchanges . The parties agree that for purposes of Section 1.7 of the Purchase Agreement (as defined in the Exchange Agreement), the value of the Series B Stock held by Investor (calculated as number of shares held by Investor multiplied by the Stated Value) will be included in the calculation of the aggregate outstanding balance of all A Notes in connection with Note Exchanges. 3. Form 8-K Disclosure . Company agrees to promptly disclose on Form 8-K its then-current number of outstanding Common Shares each time the number of outstanding Common Shares increases by five percent (5%) or more as a result of issuances of Common Shares pursuant to the Company’s ATM. 4. Conflict . In the event of a conflict between the terms and conditions contained in this Letter Agreement and those contained in the Series B Certificate, the terms and conditions contained herein shall control. 5. Transaction Document; Incorporation of Purchase Agreement Provisions . The provisions of Section 8 of the Purchase Agreement including without limitation the governing law, Arbitration Provisions (as defined the Purchase Agreement), venue, notice, fees and expenses, waiver of jury trial, and severability provisions thereof, are hereby incorporated herein by reference and shall apply to this Letter Agreement, mutatis mutandis, as if fully set forth herein, and each reference therein to “this Agreement” shall be deemed to refer to this Letter Agreement. Without limiting the foregoing, this Letter Agreement and all questions concerning its construction, validity, interpretation, enforcement and performance shall be governed by the internal laws of the State of Utah, without regard to any choice-of-law or conflict-of-law provision or rule that would cause the application of the laws of any other jurisdiction, and any dispute arising out of or relating to this Letter Agreement shall be resolved in accordance with the Arbitration Provisions. 6. Assignment; Binding upon Successors and Assigns . Company may not assign any of its rights or obligations hereunder without the prior written consent of Investor. Investor may assign its rights and obligations hereunder, in whole or in part, without the consent of Company. This Letter Agreement will be binding upon and inure to the benefit of the parties hereto and their respective successors and permitted assigns. 2 7. Amendment and Waivers . Any term or provision of this Letter Agreement may be amended and the observance of any term of this Letter Agreement may be waived (either generally or in a particular instance and either retroactively or prospectively) only by a writing signed by the parties hereto. The waiver by either party of any breach hereof or default in the performance hereof will not be deemed to constitute a waiver of any other default or any succeeding breach or default. 8. Entire Agreement . This Letter Agreement contains the entire understanding between the parties hereto with respect to the subject matter hereof and supersedes any prior understandings, agreements or representations, written or oral, relating to the subject matter hereof, other than the other Exchange Documents (as defined in the Exchange Agreement) and the Transaction Documents (as defined in the Exchange Agreement), which remain in full force and effect and are hereby ratified and confirmed. Except as expressly set forth herein, nothing in this Letter Agreement shall be deemed a waiver or modification of any right or remedy of Investor under the Exchange Documents or the Transaction Documents, all of which are expressly reserved. 9. Counterparts . This Letter Agreement may be executed in counterparts, each of which when executed and delivered shall be deemed an original and all of which, taken together, shall constitute the same agreement. This Letter Agreement may be executed by electronic signature, which shall be considered legally binding for all purposes. 10. Further Assurances . Each party to this Letter Agreement agrees to perform any further acts and execute and deliver any documents that may be reasonably necessary to carry out the provisions of this Letter Agreement. 11. Company Representations . Company represents and warrants to Investor that it has all requisite corporate power and authority to execute, deliver and perform this Letter Agreement, and this Letter Agreement has been duly authorized, executed and delivered by Company and constitutes its valid and binding obligation, enforceable against Company in accordance with its terms. [Remainder of page intentionally left blank; signature page to follow] 3 IN WITNESS WHEREOF, Investor and Company have duly executed and delivered this Letter Agreement to be effective as of the date first set forth above. INVESTOR: STREETERVILLE CAPITAL, LLC By: /s/ John Fife John Fife, President ACCEPTED AND AGREED: COMPANY: ALLARITY THERAPEUTICS, INC. By: /s/ Thomas Jensen Thomas Jensen, Chief Executive Officer [Signature Page to Letter Agreement]

title: Alpha Star Acquisition Corp
text: EX-10.1 2 ex10-1.htm EX-10.1 Exhibit 10.1 Loan Agreement This Loan Agreement (the “ Agreement ”), dated as of November 16, 2026, is entered into by and between Alpha Star Acquisition Corporation, a Cayman Islands exempted company (the “ Borrower ”), and A-Star Management Corporation, a British Virgin Islands incorporated company (the “ Lender ”). Recitals WHEREAS , the Borrower is a blank check company incorporated in the Cayman Islands on March 11, 2021. The Borrower was formed for the purpose of effecting a merger, share exchange, asset acquisition, stock purchase, reorganization, or similar business combination with one or more businesses (the “ Business Combination ”). The Lender is the sponsor of the Borrower; WHEREAS , the Borrower and the Lender entered into a loan agreement on August 26, 2024, and the Lender agreed to lend the Borrower up to US$1,500,000; WHEREAS , on September 12, 2024, the Borrower entered into a business combination agreement, as amended, with OU XDATA GROUP, a company incorporated in Estonia, and Roman Eloshvili, the sole shareholder of XDATA (the “ Merger Agreement ”); WHEREAS , the Borrower and the Lender entered into a supplemental agreement on September 25, 2024, and the Lender agreed to forfeit US$746,270 of the principal balance that would otherwise be payable by Borrower pursuant to the Loan Agreement, resulting in a remainder of US$753,730; WHEREAS , the Borrower and the Lender entered into a loan agreement on March 16, 2026, and the Lender agreed to lend the Borrower up to US$500,000; and WHEREAS , the Borrower desires to borrow from the Lender, and the Lender is willing to lend to the Borrower, up to US$500,000 on the terms and subject to the conditions set forth in this Agreement, to fund the Borrower’s working capital needs and transaction costs incurred in connection with the Business Combination. NOW, THEREFORE , in consideration of these premises and other good and valuable consideration, the parties hereto agree as follows: ARTICLE I THE LOAN 1.1. Loan . The Lender hereby agrees to extend a loan to the Borrower, from time to time, in an aggregate principal amount not to exceed Five Hundred Thousand Dollars (US$500,000) (the “ Loan ”), and the Borrower agrees to repay the outstanding principal amount of the Loan on the date on which Borrower consummates the Business Combination (the “ Maturity Date ”). The principal balance may be prepaid at any time. Under no circumstances shall any individual, including but not limited to any officer, director, employee or shareholder of the Borrower, be obligated personally for any obligations or liabilities of the Borrower hereunder. 1.2. Interest . This Loan shall be interest-free and shall not accrue any interest. 1.3. Drawdown Requests . The principal of this Agreement may be drawn down from time to time prior to the Maturity Date, upon written request from Borrower to Lender (each, a “ Drawdown Request ”). Each Drawdown Request must state the amount to be drawn down. Lender shall fund each Drawdown Request no later than five (5) business days after receipt of a Drawdown Request; provided, however, that the maximum amount of drawdowns collectively under this Agreement is Five Hundred Thousand Dollars ($500,000). Once an amount is drawn down under this Agreement, it shall not be available for future Drawdown Requests even if prepaid. No fees, payments or other amounts shall be due to Lender in connection with, or as a result of, any Drawdown Request by Borrower. It is acknowledged that the Borrower may have received amounts in respect of drawdowns under this Agreement prior to the date hereof, and it is agreed that all such sums were received as drawdowns of principal hereunder in anticipation of the execution of this Agreement. 1 It is acknowledged that (1) the Borrower may in the Drawdown Request specify that the Lender makes payments to the third parties (together with the Borrower, the “ Receiver ”) specified by the Borrower; (2) the Receiver may have received amounts in respect of the Loan under this Agreement prior to the date hereof, and it is agreed that all such sums were received in anticipation of the execution of this Agreement. 1.4. Loan Repayment . The outstanding principal amount of the Loan shall be due and payable, if not earlier paid, on the first to occur of (a) an Event of Default (as defined below), or (b) the Maturity Date. Any overdue principal shall be due and payable upon demand. 1.5. Application of Payments . All payments shall be applied first to payment in full of any costs incurred in the collection of any sum due under this Agreement, including (without limitation) reasonable attorney’s fees, then to the payment in full of any late charges and finally to the reduction of the unpaid principal balance of this Agreement. 1.6. Payments and Computations . Borrower shall make payment hereunder at maturity or otherwise not later than 5:00 p.m. (New York time) on the day when due, to Lender in immediately available funds in United States Dollars, without any setoff, defense or counterclaim, deduction or withholding of any kind (including in respect of any taxes, duties, charges or levies), except as required by applicable law. Borrower’s obligations hereunder shall not be discharged or satisfied by any tender, or any recovery pursuant to any judgment, which is expressed in or converted into any currency other than United States Dollars, except to the extent that such tender or recovery shall result in the actual receipt by Lender the full amount of United States Dollars of all amounts due hereunder. 1.7. Optional Prepayment . The Borrower may elect to prepay the entire Loan outstanding or any part of it without any penalty or prepayment fee. ARTICLE II REPRESENTATIONS AND WARRANTIES OF THE BORROWER The Borrower hereby makes the following representations and warranties, all of which shall be deemed to be continuing representations and warranties so long as any of the Loan shall remain outstanding: 2.1. Organization; Authorization . The Borrower is duly organized, validly existing and in good standing under the laws of the jurisdiction of its formation. And the Borrower has the requisite power and authority to enter into and perform this Agreement. The execution, delivery and performance of this Agreement by the Borrower and the consummation by Borrower of the transactions contemplated hereby have been duly authorized by all necessary Borrower action. This Agreement has been duly authorized, executed and delivered by Borrower and constitutes, or shall constitute when executed and delivered, a valid and binding obligation of Borrower, enforceable against Borrower in accordance with the terms thereof. 2.2. No Conflict . The execution, delivery and performance of this Agreement and the consummation by Borrower of the transactions contemplated hereby do not and will not result in a violation of Borrower’s amended and restated memorandum and articles of association or other organizational documents, as applicable. 2.3. No Untrue Statements . All statements, representations and warranties made by Borrower or any other person in this Agreement and any other agreement, document, certificate or instrument previously furnished or to be furnished by said person to Lender (i) are and shall be true, correct and complete in all material respects, at the time they were made and on and as of the date of each Loan, (ii) do not and shall not contain any untrue statement of a material fact, and (iii) do not and shall not omit to state a material fact necessary in order to make the information contained herein or therein not misleading or incomplete. 2 ARTICLE III REPRESENTATIONS AND WARRANTIES OF THE LENDER The Lender hereby makes the following representations and warranties, all of which shall be deemed to be continuing representations and warranties so long as any of the Loan shall remain outstanding: 3.1. Organization; Authorization . The Lender is duly organized, validly existing and in good standing under the laws of the jurisdiction of its formation. And the Lender has the requisite power and authority to enter into and perform this Agreement. The execution, delivery and performance of this Agreement by the Lender and the consummation by Lender of the transactions contemplated hereby have been duly authorized by all necessary Lender action. This Agreement has been duly authorized, executed and delivered by Lender and constitutes, or shall constitute when executed and delivered, a valid and binding obligation of Lender, enforceable against Lender in accordance with the terms thereof. 3.2. No Conflict . The execution, delivery and performance of this Agreement and the consummation by Lender of the transactions contemplated hereby do not and will not result in a violation of Lender’s amended and restated memorandum and articles of association or other organizational documents, as applicable. 3.3. No Untrue Statements . All statements, representations and warranties made by Lender or any other person in this Agreement and any other agreement, document, certificate or instrument previously furnished or to be furnished by said person to Borrower (i) are and shall be true, correct and complete in all material respects, at the time they were made and on and as of the date of each Loan, (ii) do not and shall not contain any untrue statement of a material fact, and (iii) do not and shall not omit to state a material fact necessary in order to make the information contained herein or therein not misleading or incomplete. ARTICLE IV EVENTS OF DEFAULT AND CONSEQUENCE 4.1 Events of Default . The following shall constitute an event of default (“ Event of Default ”): (a) Failure to Make Required Payments . Failure by Borrower to pay the principal amount due pursuant to this Agreement within five (5) business days of the date specified above. (b) Voluntary Bankruptcy, Etc . The commencement by Borrower of a voluntary case under any applicable bankruptcy, insolvency, reorganization, rehabilitation or other similar law, or the consent by it to the appointment of or taking possession by a receiver, liquidator, assignee, trustee, custodian, sequestrator (or other similar official) of Borrower or for any substantial part of its property, or the making by it of any assignment for the benefit of creditors, or the failure of Borrower generally to pay its debts as such debts become due, or the taking of corporate action by Borrower in furtherance of any of the foregoing. (c) Involuntary Bankruptcy, Etc . The entry of a decree or order for relief by a court having jurisdiction in the premises in respect of Borrower in an involuntary case under any applicable bankruptcy, insolvency or other similar law, or appointing a receiver, liquidator, assignee, custodian, trustee, sequestrator (or similar official) of Borrower or for any substantial part of its property, or ordering the winding-up or liquidation of its affairs, and the continuance of any such decree or order unstayed and in effect for a period of 60 consecutive days. 4.2 Remedies . In case any Event of Default shall have occurred, the Borrower shall promptly take any and all necessary actions to cure the default; in the event that the Borrower fails to cure the default, Lender may take the following actions: (a) Upon the occurrence of an Event of Default specified in Section 4.1(a) hereof, Lender may, by written notice to Borrower, declare this Agreement to be due immediately and payable, whereupon the unpaid principal amount of this Agreement, and all other amounts payable hereunder, shall become immediately due and payable without presentment, demand, protest or other notice of any kind, all of which are hereby expressly waived, anything contained herein or in the documents evidencing the same to the contrary notwithstanding. (b) Upon the occurrence of an Event of Default specified in Sections 4.1(b) and 4.1(c) , the unpaid principal balance of this Agreement, and all other sums payable with regard to this Agreement, shall automatically and immediately become due and payable, in all cases without any action on the part of Lender. 3 ARTICLE V MISCELLANEOUS 5.1 Entire Agreement; Modification or Amendment . This Agreement and other related documents are intended by the parties as the final, complete and exclusive statement of the transactions evidenced by this Agreement. All prior or contemporaneous promises, agreements and understandings, whether oral or written, are deemed to be superseded by this Agreement, and no party is relying on any promise, agreement or understanding not set forth in this Agreement. This Agreement may not be amended or modified except by a written instrument describing such amendment or modification executed by Borrower and Lender. 5.2 Notices . All notices, statements or other documents which are required or contemplated by this Agreement shall be made in writing and delivered: (i) personally or sent by first-class registered or certified mail, overnight courier service or facsimile or electronic transmission to the address designated in writing, (ii) by facsimile to the number most recently provided to such party or such other address or fax number as may be designated in writing by such party or (iii) by electronic mail, to the electronic mail address most recently provided to such party or such other electronic mail address as may be designated in writing by such party. Any notice or other communication so transmitted shall be deemed to have been given on the day of delivery, if delivered personally, on the business day following receipt of written confirmation, if sent by facsimile or electronic transmission, one (1) business day after delivery to an overnight courier service or five (5) days after mailing if sent by mail. 5.3 Construction . This Agreement and the rights and obligations of the parties hereunder shall be construed and interpreted in accordance with the laws of the State of New York (excluding the laws applicable to conflicts or choice of law). 5.4 Jurisdiction . ANY SUIT FOR THE ENFORCEMENT OF THIS AGREEMENT SHALL BE BROUGHT IN THE COURTS OF THE STATE OF NEW YORK OR ANY FEDERAL COURT SITTING THEREIN AND CONSENTS TO THE NONEXCLUSIVE JURISDICTION OF SUCH COURT AND SERVICE OF PROCESS. THE PARTIES HEREBY WAIVE ANY OBJECTION THAT IT MAY NOW OR HEREAFTER HAVE TO THE VENUE OF ANY SUCH SUIT OR ANY SUCH COURT OR THAT SUCH SUIT IS BROUGHT IN AN INCONVENIENT FORUM. THE PARTIES HEREBY KNOWINGLY, VOLUNTARILY AND INTENTIONALLY WAIVE THE RIGHT TO A TRIAL BY JURY IN RESPECT OF ANY CLAIM BASED HEREON, ARISING OUT OF, UNDER OR IN CONNECTION WITH THIS AGREEMENT CONTEMPLATED TO BE EXECUTED IN CONNECTION HEREWITH OR ANY COURSE OF CONDUCT, COURSE OF DEALINGS, STATEMENTS (WHETHER VERBAL OR WRITTEN) OR ACTIONS OF ANY PARTY. 5.5 Severability . Any provision contained in this Agreement, which is prohibited or unenforceable in any jurisdiction shall, as to such jurisdiction, be ineffective to the extent of such prohibition or unenforceability without invalidating the remaining provisions hereof, and any such prohibition or unenforceability in any jurisdiction shall not invalidate or render unenforceable such provision in any other jurisdiction. 5.6 Trust Waiver . Notwithstanding anything herein to the contrary, the Lender hereby waives any and all right, title, interest or claim of any kind (“ Claim ”) in or to any distribution of or from the trust account established by the Borrower in connection with its initial public offering (the “ Trust Account ”), and hereby agrees not to seek recourse, reimbursement, payment or satisfaction for any Claim against the Trust Account for any reason whatsoever. 5.7 Amendment; Waiver . Any amendment hereto or waiver of any provision hereof may be made with, and only with, the written consent of the Borrower and the Lender. 5.8 Assignment . No assignment or transfer of this Agreement or any rights or obligations hereunder may be made by any party hereto (by operation of law or otherwise) without the prior written consent of the other party hereto and any attempted assignment without the required consent shall be void. 5.9 Titles . The titles and headings indicated herein are inserted for convenience only and shall not be considered a part of this Agreement or in any way limit the construction or interpretation of this Agreement. Each of the Abrams Parties, individually, and the BCP Party, individually, is referred to herein as a “ Party ”, and all of the Abrams Parties and the BCP Party, collectively, are referred to herein as the “ Parties ”. WHEREAS, the Parties entered into that certain Voting Agreement on February 26, 2026 (the “ Voting Agreement ”); and WHEREAS, pursuant to Section 5.02 of the Voting Agreement, the Voting Agreement may be amended by written instrument executed by each of the Parties. NOW, THEREFORE, in consideration of the mutual covenants contained herein and other good and valuable consideration, the receipt and sufficiency of which are hereby acknowledged, the parties hereto agree as follows: 1. Section 2.01 of the Voting Agreement is hereby amended and restated in its entirety as follows: Section 2.01. Voting Agreement. From the date hereof until the termination of this Agreement in accordance with Section 5.03 , each Party shall vote or cause to be voted (including by proxy or written consent, if applicable) all Company Common Stock, including, for the avoidance of doubt, any shares of New Company Common Stock, owned (whether beneficially or of record) at such time by such Party: a) to cause the Board to be comprised of not fewer than seven (7) directors at all times; b) for the election of two (2) individuals designated by the Abrams Investors to serve as directors on the Board (such individuals, the “ Abrams Nominees ”), including as a replacement for any Abrams Nominee who has resigned or been removed from the Board; provided , that the Abrams Nominees must be previously approved by the BCP Investors in writing (such approval not to be unreasonably withheld, conditioned or delayed) and that Abrams Nominees Mr. David Abrams and Mr. Raja Bobbili shall be deemed approved by the BCP Investors; c) for the election of one (1) individual designated by the BCP Investors to serve as a director on the Board (such individual, the “ BCP Nominee ”), including as a replacement for any BCP Nominee who has resigned or been removed from the Board; provided , that the BCP Nominee must at all times be Mr. Edward Goldthorpe or such other person previously approved by the Abrams Investors in writing in their sole discretion; 1 d) for the election of at least four (4) other individuals, as each Party may determine in its respective sole discretion, to serve as directors on the Board; provided , that at least three (3) of such individuals shall qualify as Independent Directors; e) against any action, proposal, transaction or agreement that would or would reasonably be expected to result in the removal of any Abrams Nominee from the Board without the prior written consent of the Abrams Investors or the BCP Nominee from the Board without the prior written consent of the BCP Investors; and f) in favor of any other matter necessary to the election of directors to, or removal of directors from, the Board in accordance with this Section 2.01 (clauses (a) through (f) of this Section 2.01 , the “ Required Votes ”). 2. Section 5.03 of the Voting Agreement is hereby amended to replace the phrase “the BCP Nominees do not” with the phrase “the BCP Nominee does not”. 3. Each reference in the Voting Agreement to “this Agreement,” “hereunder,” “hereof,” “herein” or words of like import, and each reference to the Voting Agreement in any other agreement, document or instrument, shall mean and be a reference to the Voting Agreement as modified by this First Amendment. 4. This First Amendment may be executed in one or more counterparts with the effect as if the parties executing the several counterparts had all executed one counterpart, but in such event each such counterpart shall constitute an original and all of such counterparts shall together constitute one and the same instrument. 5. Except as expressly set forth in this First Amendment, the Voting Agreement remains unchanged and in full force and effect, and the Parties hereby ratify and confirm it. 2 IN WITNESS WHEREOF, the Parties hereto have caused this First Amendment to be duly executed as of the day and year first above written. EXECUTIVE SEVERANCE AND CHANGE IN CONTROL AGREEMENT This Executive Severance and Change in Control Agreement (the “ Agreement ”) is made and entered into by and between Mark Ward (the “ Executive ”) and ContextLogic Holdings Inc., a Delaware corporation (the “ Company ”), effective as of the date specified in Section 1 below. This Agreement provides severance and acceleration benefits in connection with certain qualifying terminations of the Executive’s employment with the Company. Certain capitalized terms are defined in Section 7. The Company and the Executive agree as follows: 1. Term. This Agreement shall become effective on November 16, 2026 (the “ Effective Date ”). Unless terminated sooner by written agreement of the parties pursuant to Section 6(a), this Agreement will terminate automatically on the second anniversary of the Effective Date. 2. Severance Benefits. (a) Termination Not Involving a Change in Control. If the Executive is subject to an Involuntary Termination which occurs more than three months prior to a Change in Control (if any) or more than twelve months after a Change in Control and the Executive satisfies the conditions described in Section 2(c) below, then the Executive shall be entitled to the following severance benefits: (i) a lump-sum cash severance payment equal to six (6) months of the Executive’s Base Salary, (ii) an additional lump-sum cash payment equal to six (6) months of the Executive’s benefits premiums, and (iii) unless the Company provides otherwise when an equity award is granted, the unvested portion of each outstanding time-based equity award that the Executive holds as of the Involuntary Termination that would have vested during the Executive’s completion of an additional twelve (12) months of employment following the Involuntary Termination will vest and, if applicable, become exercisable. In the case of equity awards subject to performance conditions, whether such awards are eligible for acceleration in connection with such an Involuntary Termination will be determined at the time of grant of the equity award and set forth in the equity award agreement evidencing such awards. (b) Involuntary Termination Involving a Change in Control. If the Executive is subject to an Involuntary Termination which occurs within three months prior to, or twelve months following, a Change in Control and the Executive satisfies the conditions described in Section 2(c) below, then, in lieu of the benefits provided in Section 2(a) above, the Executive shall be entitled to the following severance benefits: (i) a lump-sum cash severance payment equal to twelve (12) months of the Executive’s Base Salary, (ii) an additional lump-sum cash payment equal to twelve (12) months of the Executive’s benefits premiums, and (iii) unless the Company provides Page 1 Execution Version otherwise when an equity award is granted, one hundred percent of the unvested portion of each outstanding time-based equity award that the Executive holds as of the Involuntary Termination will vest and, if applicable, become exercisable. In the case of equity awards subject to performance conditions, whether such awards are eligible for acceleration in connection with such an Involuntary Termination will be determined at the time of grant of the equity award and set forth in the equity award agreement evidencing such awards. For avoidance of doubt, if the Executive is subject to an Involuntary Termination that occurs within three months prior to a Change in Control, the portion of the Executive’s then-outstanding and unvested equity awards that is eligible to vest and become exercisable pursuant to clause (iii) will remain outstanding for three months or until the occurrence of a Change in Control, whichever is sooner, so that any additional benefits due pursuant to clause (iii) may be provided if a Change in Control occurs within three months after the Executive’s Involuntary Termination, provided that in no event will any of the Executive’s stock options remain outstanding beyond the option’s maximum term to expiration. If a Change in Control does not occur within three months after an Involuntary Termination, any unvested portion of the Executive’s equity awards that remained outstanding following the Executive’s Involuntary Termination will immediately and automatically be forfeited. (c) Preconditions to Severance and Change in Control Benefits / Timing of Benefits. As a condition to the Executive’s receipt of any benefits described in Section 2, the Executive shall execute and allow to become effective the Company’s then-standard general release of claims, comply with the Executive’s continuing obligations (including the return of Company property) to the Company, and immediately resign from all positions the Executive holds with the Company, including as a member of the Board. The Executive must execute and return the release on or before the date specified by the Company, which will in no event be later than 50 days after the date on which the Executive’s employment terminates. If the Executive fails to return the release by the deadline or if the Executive revokes the release, then the Executive will not be entitled to the benefits described in this Section 2. All such benefits will be paid or provided within 60 days after the Executive’s Involuntary Termination or, if later, the date a Change in Control occurs. If such 60-day period spans calendar years, then payment will in any event be made in the second calendar year. 3. Section 409A. The Company intends that all payments and benefits provided under this Agreement or otherwise are exempt from, or comply with, the requirements of Section 409A of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986, as amended (the “ Code ”) so that none of the payments or benefits will be subject to the additional tax imposed under Code Section 409A, and any ambiguities herein will be interpreted in accordance with such intent. For purposes of Code Section 409A, each payment, installment or benefit payable under this Agreement is hereby designated as a separate payment. In addition, if the Company determines that the Executive is a “specified employee” under Code Page 2 Execution Version Section 409A(a)(2)(B)(i) at the time of the Executive’s Separation, then (i) any severance payments or benefits, to the extent that they are subject to Code Section 409A, will not be paid or otherwise provided until the first business day following (A) expiration of the six-month period measured from the Executive’s Separation or (B) the date of the Executive’s death and (ii) any installments that otherwise would have been paid or provided prior to such date will be paid or provided in a lump sum when the severance payments or benefits commence. The provisions of Section 7 of the Employment Agreement are incorporated by reference. 4. Section 280G. Notwithstanding anything contained in this Agreement to the contrary, in the event that the payments and benefits provided pursuant to this Agreement, together with all other payments and benefits received or to be received by the Executive (“ Payments ”), constitute “parachute payments” within the meaning of Code Section 280G, and, but for this Section 4, would be subject to the excise tax imposed by Code Section 4999 (the “ Excise Tax ”), then the Payments shall be made to the Executive either (i) in full or (ii) as to such lesser amount as would result in no portion of the Payments being subject to the Excise Tax (a “ Reduced Payment ”), whichever of the foregoing amounts, taking into account applicable federal, state and local income taxes and the Excise Tax, results in the Executive’s receipt on an after-tax basis, of the greatest amount of benefits, notwithstanding that all or some portion of the Payments may be subject to the Excise Tax. If a Reduced Payment is to be made under this section, reduction of Payments will occur in the following order: reduction of cash payments, then cancellation of equity-based payments and accelerated vesting of equity awards, and then reduction of employee benefits. If accelerated vesting of equity awards is to be reduced, such acceleration of vesting will be cancelled in the reverse order of the date of grant. In the event that cash payments or other benefits are reduced, such reduction shall occur in reverse order beginning with the payments and benefits which are to be paid furthest away in time. All determinations required to be made under this Section 4 (including whether any of the Payments are parachute payments and whether to make a Reduced Payment) will be made by an independent accounting firm selected by the Company. For purposes of making the calculations required by this section, the accounting firm may make reasonable assumptions and approximations concerning applicable taxes and may rely on reasonable, good faith interpretations concerning the application of Code Sections 280G and 4999. The Company will bear the costs that the accounting firm may reasonably incur in connection with the calculations contemplated by this Section 4. The accounting firm’s determination will be binding on both the Executive and the Company absent manifest error. 5. Company’s Successors. Any successor to all or substantially all of the Company’s business and/or assets (whether pursuant to a Change in Control, direct or indirect, and whether by purchase, merger, consolidation, liquidation or otherwise) shall assume the Company’s obligations under this Agreement and agree expressly to perform the Company’s obligations under this Agreement in the same manner and to the same extent as the Company would be required to perform such obligations in the absence of a succession. Page 3 Execution Version 6. Miscellaneous Provisions. (a) Modification or Waiver. No provision of this Agreement may be modified, waived or discharged unless the modification, waiver or discharge is agreed to in writing and signed by the Executive and by an authorized officer of the Company (other than the Executive) who has been expressly authorized by the Board. No waiver by either party of any breach of, or of compliance with, any condition or provision of this Agreement by the other party shall be considered a waiver of any other condition or provision or of the same condition or provision at another time. (b) Death of Executive. In the event of the Executive’s death following an Involuntary Termination pursuant to which the Executive is entitled to receive benefits pursuant to Section 2, but prior to the full payment thereof, such unpaid amounts will remain payable to the Executive, and all such amounts, unless otherwise provided herein, shall be paid in accordance with the terms herein to the Executive’s estate. (c) Integration. This Agreement, together with the Employment Agreement, represents the entire agreement and understanding between the parties as to the subject matter herein and supersedes all prior or contemporaneous agreements, whether written or oral, with respect to the subject matter of this Agreement. (d) Choice of Law. The validity, interpretation, construction and performance of this Agreement shall be governed by the internal substantive laws, but not the conflicts of law rules, of the State of Florida. The provisions of Section 14 of the Employment Agreement are incorporated herein by reference. (e) Tax Withholding. Any payments provided for hereunder are subject to reduction to reflect applicable withholding and payroll taxes and other reductions required under federal, state or local law. (f) Notices. Any notice required by the terms of this Agreement shall be given in writing. It shall be deemed effective upon (i) personal delivery, (ii) deposit with the United States Postal Service, by registered or certified mail, with postage and fees prepaid or (iii) deposit with Federal Express Corporation, with shipping charges prepaid. Notice shall be addressed to the Company at its principal executive office (attention General Counsel) and to the Executive at the address that he most recently provided to the Company in accordance with this Subsection (f). Page 4 Execution Version (g) Severability. The invalidity or unenforceability of any provision or provisions of this Agreement shall not affect the validity or enforceability of any other provision hereof, which shall remain in full force and effect. (h) Counterparts. This Agreement may be executed in counterparts, each of which shall be deemed an original, but all of which together will constitute one and the same instrument. 7. Definitions. Capitalized terms used but not defined in this Agreement shall have the meanings set forth in the Employment Agreement. The following terms referred to in this Agreement shall have the following meanings: (a) “Base Salary” has the meaning set forth in the Employment Agreement; provided, however, that in the event of a Resignation for Good Reason due to a material reduction in the Executive’s base salary, “Base Salary” means the Executive’s annual base salary as in effect immediately prior to such reduction or as in effect immediately prior to a Change in Control, whichever is greater. (b) “Change in Control” means: (i) Any “person” (as such term is used in Sections 13(d) and 14(d) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, as amended (the “ Exchange Act ”)) other than Abrams Capital Management, LLC and/or any of its affiliates becomes the “beneficial owner” (as defined in Rule 13d-3 of the Exchange Act), directly or indirectly, of securities of the Company representing more than 50% of the total voting power represented by the Company’s then-outstanding voting securities; (ii) The consummation of the sale or disposition by the Company of all or substantially all of the Company’s assets; (iii) The consummation of a merger or consolidation of the Company with or into any other entity, other than a merger or consolidation which would result in the voting securities of the Company outstanding immediately prior thereto continuing to represent (either by remaining outstanding or by being converted into voting securities of the surviving entity or its parent) more than 50% of the total voting power represented by the voting securities of the Company or such surviving entity or its parent outstanding immediately after such merger or consolidation; or (iv) Individuals who are members of the Company’s board of directors (the “ Incumbent Board ”) cease for any reason to constitute at least a majority of the members of the Company’s board of directors over a period of 12 months; provided, however, that if the appointment or election (or nomination for election) of any new board member was approved or recommended by a majority vote of the members of the Incumbent Board then still in office, such new member shall, for purposes of this Agreement, be considered as a member of the Incumbent Board. Page 5 Execution Version A transaction shall not constitute a Change in Control if its sole purpose is to change the state of the Company’s incorporation or to create a holding company that will be owned in substantially the same proportions by the persons who held the Company’s securities immediately before such transaction. In addition, if a Change in Control constitutes a payment event with respect to any amount which is subject to Code Section 409A, then the transaction must also constitute a “change in control event” as defined in Treasury Regulation Section 1.409A-3(i)(5) to the extent required by Code Section 409A. (c) “Employment Agreement” means the Employment Agreement made and entered into by and between the Executive and the Company, effective as of November 16, 2026. (d) “Involuntary Termination” means either (i) a Termination Without Cause or (ii) a Resignation for Good Reason. (e) “Resignation for Good Reason” means a Separation as a result of the Executive’s resignation for Good Reason. (f) “Separation” means a “separation from service” as defined in the regulations under Code Section 409A. (g) “Termination Without Cause” means a Separation as a result of the termination of the Executive’s employment by the Company without Cause and not as a result of the Executive’s death or disability. Page 6 Execution Version IN WITNESS WHEREOF, each of the parties has executed this Agreement, in the case of the Company by its duly authorized officer, as of the day and year indicated below. COMPANY CONTEXTLOGIC HOLDINGS INC. By: /s/ Raja Bobbili Name: Raja Bobbili Title: Chairman Date: 11/16/2026 EXECUTIVE By: /s/ Mark Ward Name: Mark Ward Date: 11/16/2026 Page 7

text: EX-10.1 2 ex_1047058.htm EXHIBIT 10.1 ex_1047058.htm Exhibit 10.1 EXCHANGE AGREEMENT This Exchange Agreement (this “ Agreement ”) is dated as of November 13, 2026, among SPAR Group, Inc., a Delaware corporation (the “ Company ”); SPAR Marketing Force Inc., a Nevada corporation and wholly owned subsidiary of the Company (“ SPM ”); ReposiTrak, Inc., a Nevada corporation (“ TRAK ”); and PC Group, Inc., a Utah corporation and wholly owned subsidiary of TRAK (“ PCG ”). TRAK, PCG and any affiliate thereof shall hereinafter be referred to as a “ TRAK Party ”. RECITALS A. The Company owes PCG (the “ Noteholder ”) principal and accrued interest under the Amended and Restated Senior Unsecured Promissory Note held by the Noteholder in the amount of approximately $4.0 million as of the date of this Agreement (the “ Note ”); B. TRAK and PCG also beneficially own 8,900,406 shares of the Company’s common stock, par value $0.01 per share (“ Common Stock ”) (the “ Existing Shares ”); C. TRAK and PCG have offered to cancel and terminate all Outstanding Indebtedness (as defined in Section 1.1) under the terms of the Note (i) in exchange for (A) shares of a new series of preferred stock of the Company, Series C Convertible Preferred Stock, $0.01 par value (“ Series C Preferred ”) (the “ Note Exchange ”), and (B) the Warrant (as defined in Section 3); and (C) exchange all Existing Shares for Series C Preferred and the Warrant (“ Common Exchange ” and together with the Note Exchange, the “ Exchanges ”), each under the terms and conditions set forth below in this Agreement; D. In connection with the Note Exchange and Common Exchange, TRAK has agreed to provide a $1.5 million credit facility to the Company on the terms and conditions set forth in Exhibit A to this Agreement (“ Credit Agreement ”); and E. As of the date of this Agreement, the Company owes TRAK approximately $1,105,800, separate from and in addition to the Outstanding Indebtedness under the Note (together with all interest, fees and other amounts accrued or accruing thereon, the “ Existing TRAK Obligations ”), which the parties intend to remain outstanding and payable in full, unaffected by this Agreement and the transactions contemplated thereby; and F. The Parties desire to consummate the Note Exchange and the Common Exchange, and enter into such other agreements, each on the terms and conditions set forth in this Agreement. AGREEMENT For good and valuable consideration, the parties hereto agree as follows: 1. The Exchanges 1.1 Note Exchange. At the Closing, the Noteholder will surrender the Note and all principal and accrued and unpaid interest owed under it as of the Closing Date (the “ Outstanding Indebtedness ”). In exchange, the Company will issue to the Noteholder a number of shares of Series C Preferred equal to the Outstanding Indebtedness divided by the Stated Value, as defined below. On that issuance, the Note shall be paid in full and cancelled, and neither the Company nor SPM shall have any further obligation to PCG under the terms of the Note. The parties expect the Outstanding Indebtedness to be approximately $4,000,000 on the Closing Date, with the exact amount to be confirmed in writing by the parties before the Closing. 1.2 Common Exchange . At the Closing, TRAK and PCG will sell, assign and transfer to the Company all Existing Shares in exchange for the issuance by the Company to TRAK (or as TRAK directs between itself and PCG) a number of shares of Series C Preferred with an aggregate Stated Value equal to $3,359,605 (subject to Section 1.4). Upon issuance of the Series C Preferred to TRAK, the Existing Shares will be cancelled. 1.3 Future Obligations . After the Closing, TRAK may, from time to time by written notice to the Company, exchange all or part of any amounts the Company or SPM then owes TRAK (“ Future Obligations ”) for shares of Series C Preferred having an aggregate Stated Value equal to the amount of the Future Obligations so exchanged, subject to Section 1.4. The Company will issue the additional shares of Series C Preferred issuable in exchange for Future Obligations within five (5) business days after the notice, and the exchanged amount will then be paid in full. 1.4 Fractional Shares. Series C Preferred shall not be issued in fractions of a share. Any fraction of a share of Series C Preferred that would otherwise be issuable under this Agreement shall be rounded up to the next whole share, consistent with the Certificate of Designations. 1.5 Anti-Dilution. For so long as TRAK or any of its affiliates holds any Series C Preferred, the following shall apply: 1.5.1 Issuance of Additional Shares. If the Company issues or sells any shares of Common Stock or any rights, options, warrants or other securities directly or indirectly convertible into or exercisable or exchangeable for Common Stock (“ Convertible Securities ”) (each, a “ Dilutive Issuance ”), then within five (5) business days after the Dilutive Issuance the Company shall issue to TRAK (or to such of its affiliates as TRAK directs), without further consideration, a number of additional shares of Series C Preferred (the “ Anti-Dilution Shares ”) such that the TRAK Percentage immediately after the Dilutive Issuance and the issuance of the Anti-Dilution Shares equals the TRAK Percentage immediately before the Dilutive Issuance. Each of the following shall constitute a Dilutive Issuance, notwithstanding that the securities are issued to TRAK or any of its affiliates: (A) any issuance of Series C Preferred under the Credit Agreement, whether on conversion of amounts outstanding under the Credit Agreement, as consideration for any Sourced Financing (as defined in the Credit Agreement) or otherwise; (B) any issuance of Common Stock on exercise of the Warrant or of any warrant issued under the Credit Agreement; and (C) any issuance of Series C Preferred as dividends or for Future Obligations. 1.5.2 Calculation. The number of Anti-Dilution Shares to be issued for each Dilutive Issuance shall equal (P × N × CP) ÷ ((1 − P) × SV), where “P” is the TRAK Percentage immediately before the Dilutive Issuance (expressed as a decimal); “N” is the number of shares of Common Stock issued in the Dilutive Issuance, together with the maximum number of shares of Common Stock issuable on conversion, exercise or exchange of any Convertible Securities issued in the Dilutive Issuance; “CP” is the Conversion Price then in effect; and “SV” is the Stated Value. 1.5.3 Definitions. “ TRAK Percentage ” means, at any time, a fraction, expressed as a percentage, (i) the numerator of which is the sum of all shares of Common Stock then held by TRAK and its affiliates and all Conversion Shares issuable on conversion of all Series C Preferred then held by TRAK and its affiliates, and (ii) the denominator of which is the sum of all shares of Common Stock then outstanding, all Conversion Shares issuable on conversion of all Series C Preferred then outstanding, and the maximum number of shares of Common Stock issuable on conversion, exercise or exchange of all Convertible Securities issued in prior Dilutive Issuances and then outstanding. The TRAK Percentage shall be calculated without regard to the beneficial ownership limitation in Section 2.3, the Voting Cap or any other limitation on conversion or voting. “ Credit Agreement ” means the Revolving Credit Agreement between the Company and TRAK described in Recital D and Exhibit A , as amended from time to time. 1.5.4 Excluded Issuances. The Parties agree and acknowledge that, notwithstanding anything to the contrary herein, the issuance of Common Stock upon conversion of Series C Preferred and the issuance of Anti-Dilution Shares shall each constitute a Dilutive Issuance for purposes of this Section 1.5. No issuance of equity securities to TRAK or its affiliates shall be excluded solely because TRAK or such affiliate is the recipient of such securities. 1.5.5 Notice, Terms. The Company shall give TRAK written notice of each Dilutive Issuance within two (2) business days after it occurs, setting out in reasonable detail the securities issued and the Company’s calculation of the Anti-Dilution Shares. Each Anti-Dilution Share shall have the same Stated Value, rights, preferences and privileges as each other share of Series C Preferred. 1.5.6 Authorized Shares. The Company shall at all times keep designated under the Certificate of Designations, and authorized and reserved, a sufficient number of shares of Series C Preferred and Common Stock to permit the issuance of all Anti-Dilution Shares and the conversion of all Anti-Dilution Shares into Common Stock, and shall take all corporate action necessary to do so; provided that, until the amendment described in Section 8.5 becomes effective, the Company’s obligations under this Section 1.5.6 as to Common Stock shall be satisfied by compliance with Section 2.8. 1.6 Existing TRAK Obligations. Nothing in this Agreement, the Certificate of Designations, the Warrant, the Credit Agreement or any transaction contemplated by any of them shall forgive, release, discharge, reduce, convert, exchange, subordinate or otherwise impair the Existing TRAK Obligations, all of which shall remain outstanding and payable in full in accordance with their terms; provided that TRAK may, in its sole discretion, elect to exchange all or any part of the Existing TRAK Obligations for Series C Preferred under Section 1.3. The Company acknowledges that the Existing TRAK Obligations are valid and owing and are not subject to any defense, offset or counterclaim. 1.7 Ownership Cap. Notwithstanding anything to the contrary in this Agreement, the Certificate of Designations, the Warrant, the Credit Agreement, any warrant issued under the Credit Agreement or any other agreement or instrument relating to any of them (collectively, the “Transaction Documents”), in no event shall (a) the Common Percentage exceed 50% at any time, or (b) the TRAK Parties cast, or have counted, more than 50% of the votes cast and counted on any matter, which shall be limited as provided in the Voting Cap (together, the “ Ownership Cap ”). Notwithstanding the foregoing, the Ownership Cap, this Section 1.7, Section 2.3, the Voting Cap and every other limitation in any Transaction Document on the Common Percentage, on the beneficial ownership of Common Stock by the TRAK Parties or on the votes that the TRAK Parties may cast shall terminate and cease to apply on December 23, 2027 (the “ Sunset Date ”). On and after the Sunset Date, the TRAK Parties may convert, exercise, exchange and acquire securities of the Company, and vote all of them, without regard to any such limitation, even if as a result the TRAK Parties hold more than 50% of the outstanding Common Stock or of the voting power of the Company. The termination of this Section 1.7 does not validate any issuance, transfer or acquisition that violated it before the Sunset Date. 1.7.1 Definitions. “TRAK Parties” means TRAK, PCG, each of their affiliates, and each other person whose beneficial ownership of Common Stock would be aggregated with that of TRAK or PCG for purposes of Section 13(d) of the Exchange Act, including as a member of a “group.” “Common Percentage” means, at any time, a fraction, expressed as a percentage, (i) the numerator of which is the number of shares of Common Stock then held of record or beneficially owned (within the meaning of Rule 13d-3 under the Exchange Act) by the TRAK Parties, excluding Common Stock issuable on conversion of Series C Preferred or on exercise of the Warrant or any other warrant, option or right until it is issued, and (ii) the denominator of which is the number of shares of Common Stock then outstanding. 1.7.2 Limitation on Conversions, Exercises and Acquisitions. The Company shall not issue or transfer any Common Stock to any TRAK Party, and TRAK shall not, and shall cause each other TRAK Party not to, acquire any Common Stock (whether from the Company or any other person, and whether by conversion, exercise, purchase, exchange or otherwise), to the extent that, immediately after giving effect to the issuance or acquisition, the Common Percentage would exceed 50%. Without limiting the foregoing, this Section 1.7.2 applies to (a) any conversion of Series C Preferred; (b) any exercise of the Warrant or of any warrant issued under the Credit Agreement; (c) any other issuance of Common Stock under any Transaction Document; and (d) any purchase or other acquisition of Common Stock by a TRAK Party from any other person. 1.7.3 Effect of Limitation. To the extent a conversion or exercise is limited by Section 1.7.2, (a) the Series C Preferred, the Warrant or the other warrant, as applicable, shall remain outstanding and convertible or exercisable in accordance with its terms, subject to this Section 1.7; (b) no exercise price shall be payable for any shares not issued; and (c) any fractional share of Common Stock that would otherwise be rounded up shall instead be rounded down if rounding up would cause the Common Percentage to exceed 50%. 1.7.4 Company Actions; Excess Shares. The Company shall not redeem, repurchase or otherwise acquire any shares of Common Stock, or take any other action, if immediately after giving effect to it the Common Percentage would exceed 50%. If, notwithstanding this Section 1.7, the Common Percentage exceeds 50% at any time for any reason, then within five business days, TRAK shall exchange with the Company, and the Company shall accept, the smallest whole number of shares of Common Stock held by the TRAK Parties necessary to reduce the Common Percentage to 50% or less for shares of Series C Preferred having an aggregate Stated Value equal to that number of shares multiplied by the Conversion Price then in effect, and until that exchange is completed the excess shares shall be subject to the Voting Cap and shall not be voted or counted. 1.7.5 Calculations. Before each conversion, exercise or other issuance of Common Stock to a TRAK Party, the Company shall calculate the Common Percentage, using the number of outstanding shares of Common Stock reported by its transfer agent as of a date not more than two business days earlier, and shall deliver its calculation to TRAK. TRAK shall promptly provide any information the Company reasonably requests about Common Stock held by the TRAK Parties, and shall not acquire Common Stock from any other person without first confirming with the Company that the acquisition complies with this Section 1.7. 1.7.6 Void Issuances. Any issuance, transfer or acquisition of Common Stock in violation of this Section 1.7 shall be null and void ab initio to the extent of the excess. The Company shall not register or recognize, and shall instruct its transfer agent not to register or recognize, any Common Stock issued, transferred or acquired in violation of this Section 1.7, and no vote in respect of any such Common Stock shall be cast or counted. 1.7.7 Priority; Conforming Documents. To the extent any provision of Exhibit A (Credit Agreement), including any warrant issued under it, Exhibit B (Form of Series C Preferred Certificate of Designations), including the Certificate of Designations as filed, or Exhibit C (Form of Warrant), including the Warrant as issued, would permit or result in the Common Percentage exceeding 50% or the TRAK Parties casting or having counted more than 50% of the votes cast and counted on any matter, the terms of this Section 1.7 control, notwithstanding any conflict between this Section 1.7 and that provision and notwithstanding the introductory paragraph of Section 2 or any provision of an exhibit stating that it controls. This Section 1.7 also controls over any conflicting provision of any other Transaction Document. The Company and TRAK shall cause the Certificate of Designations, the Warrant, the Credit Agreement and each warrant issued under the Credit Agreement to contain provisions consistent with this Section 1.7. No amendment or waiver of this Section 1.7 shall be effective unless approved by a majority of the Company’s disinterested directors. 2. The Series C Preferred shall vote together with the Common Stock as a single class on all matters. Each share of Series C Preferred is entitled to a number of votes equal to the number of whole shares of Common Stock into which it is then convertible (determined by dividing its Stated Value by the Conversion Price then in effect), and each share of Common Stock has one vote; provided, however , notwithstanding anything to the contrary herein, on any matter on which holders of Series C Preferred are entitled to vote together with holders of Common Stock as a single class, no holder of Series C Preferred (together with its affiliates and any other persons whose beneficial ownership would be aggregated with such holder’s for purposes of Section 13(d) of the Exchange Act) shall be entitled to cast votes, whether in respect of Preferred Stock, Common Stock or any other voting securities, in excess of 50% of the sum of (x) the votes cast and counted on such matter by such holder and such persons and (y) the total votes entitled to be cast on such matter by all other holders of voting securities, so that such holder and such persons may in no event cast more than 50% of the votes that may be cast and counted on such matter (the “ Voting Cap ”). TRAK’s obligations under this Section 10 are secondary to, and in excess of, (a) all directors’ and officers’ liability insurance maintained by the Company or any of its subsidiaries (the “ D&O Insurance ”), and (b) the Company’s obligations to indemnify and advance expenses to its directors and officers under its certificate of incorporation (the “ Charter Indemnification ”). Accordingly, TRAK shall be obligated to pay a Loss only to the extent it exceeds the sum of all amounts paid for that Loss under the D&O Insurance and under the Charter Indemnification, and only after (i) the applicable limits of the D&O Insurance have been exhausted by payment, or each applicable insurer has denied coverage for that Loss in writing, and (ii) the Company has paid all amounts that it is required, and permitted by applicable law, to pay for that Loss under the Charter Indemnification. Losses of the Company do not include any amount the Company pays under the Charter Indemnification or any retention or deductible under the D&O Insurance. 10.3 Primary Sources . The Company shall (a) maintain D&O Insurance for at least six years after the date of this Agreement with coverage and limits no less favorable to the insureds than the D&O Insurance in effect on the date of this Agreement; (b) not amend its certificate of incorporation in any way that reduces the Charter Indemnification as it applies to any Fiduciary Claim; and (c) together with each Company Indemnified Party seeking indemnification, use commercially reasonable efforts to recover each Loss under the D&O Insurance and the Charter Indemnification before seeking payment from TRAK. 10.4 Advancement . Once the conditions in clauses (i) and (ii) of Section 10.2 have been satisfied for a Fiduciary Claim, TRAK shall advance the reasonable defense costs of each Company Indemnified Party who is or was a director or officer for that Fiduciary Claim within 30 days after receiving reasonably detailed invoices, subject to that person’s written undertaking to repay the amounts advanced if it is finally determined that the person is not entitled to indemnification under this Section 10. 10.5 Exclusions . TRAK has no obligation under this Section 10 for any Loss (a) to the extent a court of competent jurisdiction finally determines that the Loss resulted from the Company Indemnified Party’s fraud, intentional misconduct, or receipt of a personal financial benefit to which it was not legally entitled; (b) arising from a Fiduciary Claim brought by TRAK, PCG or any of their affiliates; or (c) to the extent the Company Indemnified Party has actually received payment for that Loss from any other source. 10.6 Procedures . A Company Indemnified Party seeking indemnification shall give TRAK prompt written notice of the Fiduciary Claim, but a delay in giving notice relieves TRAK of its obligations only to the extent TRAK is materially prejudiced by the delay. The Company shall keep TRAK reasonably informed of the status of each Fiduciary Claim, and TRAK may participate in its defense at its own expense through counsel of its choice. No Company Indemnified Party may settle a Fiduciary Claim, or consent to the entry of any judgment, for which TRAK may be required to pay any amount without TRAK’s prior written consent, which TRAK will not unreasonably withhold, condition or delay. 10.7 Subrogation; Excess Position . On making any payment under this Section 10, TRAK will be subrogated to the rights of the Company Indemnified Party to recover that amount under the D&O Insurance and the Charter Indemnification, and each Company Indemnified Party shall sign the documents reasonably required to secure those rights. Neither the Company nor any Company Indemnified Party shall take the position, with any insurer or otherwise, that TRAK’s obligations under this Section 10 are primary to the D&O Insurance or the Charter Indemnification, or seek contribution or reimbursement from TRAK for any amount paid under either of them. 10.8 Third-Party Beneficiaries; Survival; Amendment . Each Company Indemnified Party that is not a party to this Agreement is an express third-party beneficiary of this Section 10 and may enforce it directly. This Section 10 survives the Closing and any termination of this Agreement until 60 days after the expiration of the statute of limitations applicable to Fiduciary Claims, and thereafter as to any Fiduciary Claim asserted before then until it is finally resolved. Despite Section 11.1, this Section 10 may not be amended or waived in a way that adversely affects any Company Indemnified Party without that person’s written consent. 11. General 11.1 Entire Agreement . This Agreement, with its exhibits, is the parties’ entire agreement on its subject and replaces the term sheet and all prior discussions. It may be amended or waived only in a writing signed by the Company and TRAK. 11.2 Further Actions . Each party will sign the documents and take the further actions reasonably needed to carry out this Agreement. 11.3 Expenses . Each party pays its own expenses. 11.4 Governing Law . Delaware law governs this Agreement. 11.5 Notices . Notices must be in writing and are effective when delivered by hand, by email with confirmation of receipt, or by overnight courier to the addresses on the signature page. 11.6 Counterparts . This Agreement may be signed in counterparts and by electronic signature, each of which is an original. 11.7 Survival . The representations and warranties in Section 7 survive the Closing for 12 months. Each covenant survives until fully performed, and Section 8 survives as stated therein. Section 10 survives as stated therein. 11.8 Assignment . No party may assign this Agreement without the written consent of the Company and TRAK, except that TRAK may assign its rights to an affiliate that agrees in writing to be bound by this Agreement. 11.9 Tax Treatment . For income tax purposes, the Series C Preferred issued for the Note will be allocated first to the principal of the Note and then to accrued but unpaid interest. The parties intend each Exchange in Section 1 to qualify as a recapitalization under Section 368(a)(1)(E) of the Internal Revenue Code, to the extent permitted by law. Each party will file its tax returns consistently with this Section unless otherwise required by a final determination of a taxing authority, and each party is responsible for its own taxes arising from the transactions.
